page: Amazon Web Services c6a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by third-generation AMD EPYC 7R13 processors. It delivers 32 virtual CPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. Memory configuration includes 64.0 GB of DDR4 system memory clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance carries 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside 0.5 MB L2 and 32 KB L1 data caches per core. Hardware cryptography extensions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI are present, while AVX-512 and matrix extensions are absent.

Hardware configurations exclude integrated local disk storage and discrete GPU accelerators, relying on remote elastic storage solutions and standard CPU execution for compute pipelines. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 12 Gbps. In benchmark tests, the instance shows strong single-core CPU throughput via stress-ng, scoring 2990.99, while multi-core stress-ng reaches 47825.07. PassMark testing records an overall CPU score of 38324.88 alongside a strong memory subsystem mark of 2774.08. Read-only cached memory bandwidth exceeds 2291 GB/sec, while uncached large-block read transfers measure 76.63 GB/sec.

Workload evaluation demonstrates solid throughput for compile tasks, static web serving at 25.98 GB/sec, and in-memory key-value operations registering 35.17 million Redis SET operations per second. Light-parameter language model generation also shows strong responsiveness on small models, though lack of accelerator hardware severely constrains larger model inference. Given its compute density and lack of bundled local NVMe storage, c6a.8xlarge offers cost-effective execution for distributed batch processing, continuous integration build servers, and web serving fleets that do not require high storage IOPS or heavy GPU acceleration.
description: Amazon Web Services c6a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 3.6 GHz AMD EPYC 7R13 processor under the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory, adhering to a 1:2 compute-focused memory allocation. It features 12 Gbps baseline networking, omitting integrated local storage and GPU accelerators. Hardware security includes AES, VAES, and SHA-NI acceleration, though AVX-512 instructions are unsupported. Benchmark results show strong single-core compute and memory performance, supported by 35.17 million Redis SET operations per second and 25.98 GB/sec static web throughput. Without local NVMe disks, storage must be attached remotely. The instance delivers cost-efficient throughput for compilation pipelines, distributed microservices, batch compute, and intermediate web serving.
